project_scope.index_source: Hays Botany ID Master Curation Tracker — Genus Study Index, row 43
project_scope.name_resolution_note: Nine source names do NOT mean nine installed species. O. lindheimeri is an accepted synonym of var. lindheimeri; O. engelmannii at species rank is a broader concept not safely assignable to the variety from a name alone; O. senilis maps to accepted O. orbiculata, a separate unresolved source row—not an installed ninth lesson species.
project_scope.status_boundary: Native range is preserved per canonical species; accession in pool does NOT confer target-zone native PASS. O. gilvescens and strict O. phaeacantha retain concept/range unresolved; O. azurea and O. rufida remain not confirmed for target zone.

shared_genus_recognition.look_here_first: Find an areole on a *flattened photosynthetic stem segment* (cladode/pad). An areole is a short-shoot cushion, often with barbed glochids and sometimes longer permanent spines; new pads, flowers and fruit also arise at areoles. First sort flat pads from Cylindropuntia's cylindrical jointed stems; THEN compare whole plant, mature pad, areoles, spine/glochid pattern, flowers and ripe fruit.

terms.definition: Flattened green stem segment, not a leaf.
Modified short shoot on a cactus; bears hairs, spines, glochids and/or flowers/branches.
Tiny barbed, detachable spine produced in an areole; may injure skin or eyes even on otherwise spineless pads.
Larger tougher cactus spine; number and size vary within species and pad age.
Stem-derived tissue surrounding the inferior ovary; exterior can bear areoles, so a flower/fruit can appear spiny.
Waxy blue-gray surface bloom; environmentally variable, and shared by several Opuntia.

shared_genus_recognition.careful_handling: Do not touch or harvest glochids barehanded. Work with no-contact macro/telephoto or suitable protective equipment; never encourage touching pads to test 'spineless' species.
shared_genus_recognition.comparison_method: Use 3 mature paddles on different branches if available; count areoles by a consistent diagonal midway across each pad, photograph side + face with ruler, note mature glochid COLOR, spine distribution across face vs distal edge, and fruit pulp color where safely visible.

visual_entry_key.prompt: Flat padded stems with areoles and barbed glochids?
visual_entry_key.action: Yes → Opuntia. Cylindrical jointed segments → examine Cylindropuntia; a leaf rosette → Agave/Yucca; no areoles → not Cactaceae.

visual_entry_key.prompt: Are mature pads essentially without long rigid permanent spines?
visual_entry_key.action: With many dense reddish-brown glochid dots, consider O. rufida but distinguish O. microdasys by pad size/areoles and fruit; spineless lindheimeri morphotypes also exist. Do NOT equate spine-free with rufida.

visual_entry_key.prompt: Are plant and pads low, radiating or close to ground, mostly small (roughly 5–11 cm)?
visual_entry_key.action: O. macrorhiza candidate. Inspect 5–8 diagonal areoles, few permanent spines and root/habit if naturally exposed. Hybrid ×edwardsii and young engelmannii can confuse.

visual_entry_key.prompt: Are pads much larger, typically ~15–30 cm, broadly round or obovate on a tall or sprawling shrub?
visual_entry_key.action: O. engelmannii var. lindheimeri candidate. Verify yellowish straight/slightly curving spines when present; never require spines because truly spineless morphotypes occur.

visual_entry_key.prompt: Is the plant low/trailing with conspicuous brown-to-gray spines and wine-red/purple fruit?
visual_entry_key.action: Strict O. phaeacantha candidate only; keep concept unresolved if no expert specimen/reference. Historic phaeacantha var. major → O. gilvescens in current Kew taxonomy.

visual_entry_key.prompt: Does a historic label or Mexican glaucous/blue-padded specimen suggest O. azurea, O. gilvescens or O. senilis?
visual_entry_key.action: STOP and verify exact accepted species concept. Blue pads, flowers and historic names alone do not resolve these; O. senilis is synonym of O. orbiculata and the source remains HOLD.

visual_entry_key.prompt: Are pad, spines, areoles and flowers/fruit incompletely documented or hybrid/intergrade traits present?
visual_entry_key.action: Use Opuntia sp. or the exact conservative complex name; do not manufacture species-level certainty from one field photo.

species_quick_profiles.name: Opuntia engelmannii var. lindheimeri
species_quick_profiles.diagnostic_bundle: Large flat broad pads + variable straight/slightly curving yellowish rigid spines (possibly none) + areoles + beet-red/purple juicy fruit. Flower/fruits and pad shape > one spine count.
species_quick_profiles.risk: Spineless forms and hybrids ×edwardsii with macrorhiza. O. lindheimeri source row maps here but O. engelmannii parent records can be broader.

species_quick_profiles.name: Opuntia macrorhiza
species_quick_profiles.diagnostic_bundle: Low clumps near ground; small pads; few spines, sometimes bent, with dense orangish-brown glochids; flowering base often reddish. Compare to young lindheimeri and ×edwardsii.
species_quick_profiles.risk: Hybridization known; O. ×edwardsii reported in Blanco and Guadalupe counties. Use conservative ID for intermediates.

species_quick_profiles.name: Opuntia phaeacantha
species_quick_profiles.diagnostic_bundle: Often trailing/spreading and brown-spined; yellow flowers with red bases and purplish fruit. This is a candidate suite, not license to transfer older phaeacantha IDs.
species_quick_profiles.risk: Historical broad varieties split among gilvescens, camanchica, spinosibacca; old source phaeacantha var. major cannot be counted here.

species_quick_profiles.name: Opuntia gilvescens
species_quick_profiles.diagnostic_bundle: Accepted separate name for older O. phaeacantha var. major usage; requires current-concept exact-specimen comparative pad, areole, spine and fruit evidence. No invented field key.
species_quick_profiles.risk: Do not mistake old phaeacantha photos for modern gilvescens without voucher/expert determination.

species_quick_profiles.name: Opuntia rufida
species_quick_profiles.diagnostic_bundle: Grayish-green mature pads with many rust-red glochid clusters, usually no rigid spines; broader pads and fewer diagonal areoles than O. microdasys in FNA.
species_quick_profiles.risk: Red or absent long spines alone insufficient; microdasys can also show reddish glochids and hybridizes in Mexico.

species_quick_profiles.name: Opuntia azurea
species_quick_profiles.diagnostic_bundle: Often glaucous blue-green branching pads and long pale rigid spines; verify exact current Mexican taxon with mature pad, areoles, spines and fruit.
species_quick_profiles.risk: Historical Texas azurea records can be O. aureispina or other glaucous taxa; wax bloom is not an ID.

lookalike_routing.name: Cylindropuntia
lookalike_routing.rule: Jointed cylindrical green stems typically with sheathed spines; Opuntia flattened pads with glochids.

lookalike_routing.name: Euphorbia, Stapelia and other succulent mimics
lookalike_routing.rule: True cactus areoles (with glochids on Opuntia), rather than mere thorns; Euphorbia cyathia/capsules differ.

lookalike_routing.name: Opuntia microdasys
lookalike_routing.rule: Mostly spineless with dense glochid dots, BUT smaller brighter green puberulent pads and 11–16 diagonal mid-pad areoles vs 8–13 in O. rufida FNA; cultivar/photo angle affects count.

lookalike_routing.name: Opuntia aureispina
lookalike_routing.rule: Texas glaucous-spined desert pricklypear that can underlie older O. azurea labels; requires specialist modern species review.

lookalike_routing.name: Opuntia ×edwardsii
lookalike_routing.rule: Hybrid of macrorhiza × engelmannii (including var. lindheimeri); FNA reports hybrid in Blanco and Guadalupe counties. Not a source-pool installed taxon; ID can remain unresolved.

lookalike_routing.name: Opuntia camanchica / O. spinosibacca
lookalike_routing.rule: Modern strict taxa potentially split from older phaeacantha sensu lato; do not relabel photographic records without vouchers.
